newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares burst higher, dollar pressured.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares burst higher, dollar pressured.

text.p: European shares were in good heart on Friday, climbing higher on the strength of another record close on Wall Street, while the dollar tried to steady against the yen but remained under pressure.
The U.S. Dow Jones industrial average set its 19th record close of the year on Thursday after blue-chip stocks overcame a bigger-than-expected rise in consumer prices last month.
The Dow ended up 47.39 points at 7,333.55 -- its first close above 7,300 -- as it eclipsed Monday's record finish of 7,292.75.
Conflicting economic news has sent mixed signals as to whether the U.S. Federal Reserve central bank would raise interest rates when its policy-making Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets on Tuesday.

"We see a 50/50 chance that the Fed may raise rates just to continue with their pre-emptive strike but the inflation numbers have looked pretty good this week," said U.S. based analyst Elaine Garzarelli, who remains bullish with a year-end target of 7,600 for the Dow.
In bullion markets, gold opened firmer at $347.50 versus London's close of $346.95. The market was very quiet, having shrugged off German plans to revalue gold, but not sell any of its holdings.
London's FTSE 100 started the last session of a record-breaking week by moving up around 0.7 percent after Wall Street's strong finish. The index was 34.6 points up at 4,715.8 by 0900 GMT.

Dealers and strategists also said the market was activity ahead of the 0930 GMT expiry of FTSE options and the index looked likely to stay around 4,700 and then drift off towards a more cautious close.
"There's nothing big until next Tuesday's FOMC meeting and the market will be biding time for the next two days," said Dresdner Kleinwort Benson strategist, Philip Isherwood.

The FTSE 100's recent record-setting advance was halted when it closed lower on Wednesday and Thursday, having set a fresh high on Tuesday of 4,720.3. The index has risen about seven percent on the back of post-election euphoria.

"The market's just a little tired at the end of a big week. Everyone knows cash balances are still high but we're seeing a big pause for breath until after next Tuesday's out of the way," said one dealer.
French stocks rose to all time highs, bolstered by gains in bond prices, Wall Street shares and a fresh Ipsos poll showing the conservatives leading in the upcoming parliamentary election.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 18.72 points, or 0.67 percent, at 2,794.73 at 0900 GMT.
German shares were around one percent higher, up 36.08 at 3,598.19, underpinned by Wall Street's close and the dollar's foray above 1.70 marks.

In currencies, the dollar traded slightly firmer against the mark and yen early in Europe as the markets stabilised following a volatile week of sharp yen gains and shifting interest rate expectations in Japan and the United States.
The rally soon faltered however and the U.S. currency stood at around 115.75 yen, well off its overnight high of 117.00 yen, and at 1.6984 marks at 0900 gmt.

Traders in Tokyo said the overnight session was dominated by a reaction to this week's steep decline in dollar/yen which was seen to be overdone. The recovery was limited and capped at 117 yen. Dollar/mark continued to outperform and held firm above 1.70 in Europe.
"Things are calmer and people seem to be digesting what was a very eventful week. We're starting to focus now on the FOMC next week," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago.

"The big question now is whether the U.S. economy has slowed enough to prevent the Fed from tightening and on balance we think they will leave rates unchanged next week," said Knuthsen. "The market has scaled back its expectations and if they do raise rates the dollar could get a boost."
The dollar/yen has collapsed from 4-1/2-year highs this month and lost almost 10 percent of its value in just two weeks.

The reversal was triggered by a barrage of verbal intervention from Japanese officials aimed at preventing the yen weakening further and hastening the need for higher Japanese interest rates. Growing speculation about a rise Japanese rates, nevertheless, has reinforced the yen recovery, said analysts.
STOCK PRICES AT 0900 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 34.6 points at 4,715.8.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 18.72 points at 2,794.73.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 36.08 points at 3,598.19.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6984 marks and 115.75 yen compared with 1.6986 marks and 116.28 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened firmer at $347.50 versus London's close of $346.95 on Thursday.
